Kodely generates a real, readable React and TypeScript codebase, and you can view and copy every generated file directly in-app. That said, be precise about what Kodely offers today: there is no zip export or download yet, so you are copying files by hand rather than pulling a full project archive. It is a meaningfully more open system than Squarespace's closed one, just not a finished one-click export experience.

17	Squarespace hosting is bundled with the subscription and includes a custom domain from day one — you can point a real domain like yourbusiness.com at it immediately. Kodely's one-click Publish puts your site live on a free <name>.kodely.site subdomain instantly, with every publish scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys first. 12	WordPress itself is free and open source. What costs money is everything around it: hosting, a domain, and often premium plugins or themes for anything beyond a basic blog. If a generation fails to compile, you are not charged for it. There is no separate hosting bill on top — publishing to your *.kodely.site URL is included.
14	Do you own the code
15	This is WordPress's clearest structural advantage. Self-hosted WordPress gives you direct file access to your themes, plugins, and database from the moment you install it. You can move hosts, fork a plugin, or edit PHP directly whenever you want.
16	Kodely generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application — genuine component files, not a locked-in page-builder format — and you can view and copy that source from inside the app. What Kodely does not have yet is a code export or zip download, so you cannot currently pull the full project out to run on your own infrastructure. If self-hosting or full portability is a requirement today, WordPress wins outright.
17	Hosting and going live
18	With WordPress, going live means choosing a host, configuring DNS, installing SSL, and keeping the server patched — or paying someone to do it. It is flexible, including custom domains from the start, but it is a real setup step.
19	With Kodely, publishing is one click. Your site goes live on a real public URL at <name>.kodely.site, free, with no separate hosting account to configure. The tradeoff is that Kodely does not support custom domains yet — you are on the kodely.site subdomain for now, which matters if branded domain hosting is non-negotiable for your launch.
20	Backend and plugin depth
21	WordPress's plugin library is its strongest asset for anything beyond a marketing page: WooCommerce for e-commerce, Gravity Forms or similar for lead capture, Yoast or Rank Math for SEO, MemberPress for gated content, and booking plugins for appointments. If your site needs a database-backed feature, there is very likely a plugin for it already.
22	Kodely currently generates frontend applications only — it does not generate backend logic, databases, authentication, or payment processing. If you need an e-commerce checkout, a login system, or a booking database today, WordPress with the right plugins is the more capable choice.
23	Maintenance burden
24	This is where Kodely's design pays off. A self-hosted WordPress site is not a one-time build — it is ongoing work. Core updates, theme updates, and plugin updates all need to happen regularly, and plugin conflicts after an update are a routine headache. Someone has to own that, indefinitely.
25	Kodely has no server to patch and no plugin stack to keep in sync, because there is no server or plugin stack exposed to you at all. Changes happen by describing them in chat, and every successful generation is a checkpoint, so rolling back a change you do not like is free and instant. There is nothing to maintain between edits.
26	Security
27	WordPress's popularity is also its biggest security liability: because so many sites run it, and because third-party plugins vary wildly in code quality, WordPress sites are one of the most common targets for automated hacking attempts, almost always through vulnerable or outdated plugins. Keeping a WordPress site secure means staying current on updates and vetting every plugin you install.
28	Kodely removes that entire attack surface for you — there is no plugin marketplace to introduce third-party vulnerabilities, and every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live.
29	Best for
30	Choose WordPress if you need e-commerce, a membership system, complex custom functionality, a custom domain immediately, or full ownership and portability of your files, and you are willing to own ongoing maintenance (or pay a host that does it for you).
31	Choose Kodely if you want a real coded site live in minutes with zero server or plugin maintenance, you are building a marketing site, landing page, portfolio, or frontend-only product, and you are comfortable on a kodely.site subdomain for now while the platform adds custom domains and export.

34	No. Kodely generates an independent Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS application from scratch for each project. It has no relationship to WordPress's codebase or plugin system.
